sentence: This project studies how searching and guarding males of two-lined salamanders keep their differences in reproductive behavior within urban streams.
This project studies the genetic changes and environmental conditions behind differences in ripe fruit color across a plant group that includes tomato, eggplant, and potato.
This project builds tools that make charged droplets so that proteins in solution can be studied with mass spectrometry while keeping their structures intact.
This project builds a tool that compares user level policy with system-level policy to find mismatches that may lead to security vulnerabilities.
This project compares tomato and rice to find out how plant root cells host beneficial fungi and how this helps plants cope with drought.
This project studies ways to shrink and compress data in AI systems so they work more efficiently without losing much accuracy.
This project watches Internet Protocol version 6 traffic passively to find outages and to learn how reliable it is and how it is used.
This project builds methods that find groups of patients and groups of cells in complex molecular data and pick out the features that define each group.
This project studies how touch and vision can work together so robots can handle fragile objects reliably.
This project builds a framework that checks that scientific computing programs stay correct despite floating-point errors.
This project brings researchers together to promote using AI to analyze high-resolution images of plant cells.
This project builds engineered proteins whose activity is controlled by magnetic fields, so that biochemical reactions in cells can be dialed up or down.
This project studies enzymes that modify peptides into bioactive organic molecules and how the enzymes recognize and bind those peptides.
This project twists one atomically thin layer against another to make an array of quantum dots and uses a near-field optical probe to address each dot individually.
This project designs devices made from nano-structured composite media that shape complex light beams at tiny sizes and very fast times to control molecular transitions.
This project builds a facility that combines powerful lasers with X-rays to study materials and molecules that change very fast.
This project uses computer simulations to study nonlinear processes in the early Universe and what they show about gravity, particle physics, and dark matter.
This project studies how central processing units can take a larger role in managing communication and data movement in large artificial intelligence systems.
